name: Cesar Andreu Iglesias
bio: Cesar Andreu Iglesias was a Puerto Rican Communist writer, one of the eleven defendants in the first Smith Act prosecution ever brought in Puerto Rico. Arrested in 1954, the group went to trial in San Juan in 1956 in an English-language proceeding most of the defendants could not follow.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
convicted: Arrested 1954; on trial in Puerto Rico (1956)
sentence: Faced a mainland prison term if convicted

name: Jane Speed de Andreu
bio: Jane Speed de Andreu was the only 'continental' defendant in the Puerto Rico Smith Act case — a white woman from an old Alabama family who had been active in Alabama sharecroppers' and anti-Jim Crow struggles before marrying Cesar Andreu Iglesias. A former Communist, she was one of the eleven indicted in San Juan.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
convicted: Arrested 1954; on trial in Puerto Rico (1956)
sentence: Faced a mainland prison term if convicted

name: Juan Emmanuelli
bio: Juan Emmanuelli was one of the eleven defendants in Puerto Rico's first Smith Act case. A former Communist no longer a party member by the time of trial, he was indicted with the others in San Juan for conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the government.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
convicted: Arrested 1954; on trial in Puerto Rico (1956)
sentence: Faced a mainland prison term if convicted

name: Jorge Maysonet-Hernandez
bio: Jorge Maysonet-Hernandez, a Puerto Rican Communist in his early forties, was one of the eleven defendants in the first Smith Act prosecution brought in Puerto Rico, tried in San Juan in 1956.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
convicted: Arrested 1954; on trial in Puerto Rico (1956)
sentence: Faced a mainland prison term if convicted

name: Consuelo Burgos
bio: Consuelo Burgos was one of two women among the eleven defendants in Puerto Rico's first Smith Act case, indicted in 1954 and tried in San Juan in 1956 for conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the government.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government

sentence: Faced a mainland prison term if convicted

name: Cristino Perez Mendez
bio: Cristino Perez Mendez was one of the eleven Puerto Rican Communists prosecuted in the island's first Smith Act case, arrested in 1954 and brought to trial in San Juan in 1956.

name: Juan Saez Corales
bio: Juan Saez Corales was a veteran Puerto Rican labor leader and Communist, a candidate for the island's House of Representatives, who campaigned under the slogan 'Jail, no; Congress, yes' while under indictment in Puerto Rico's first Smith Act case. He was one of the eleven defendants tried in San Juan in 1956.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government

sentence: Faced a mainland prison term if convicted
